artifact.title: Research synthesis
artifact.question: What did the research find, how strong is each finding and which decisions did it drive?
artifact.iDecided: The codebook structure, the ordinal evidence rubric instead of tallies and which themes became decisions.
artifact.weBuilt: The coding, two coders per source, the affinity sessions and the evidence table. Theme names were argued out in the weekly coding review.

label: Reconstructed. Every finding here is a reconstruction of what the research found, rated by an ordinal rubric. No observation, participant or quote count appears because every n except the dry run is a planned target.

codes.def: Finding where a piece of evidence lives across systems or requests.
codes.include: Any search, request or wait to obtain a document.
codes.example: Opening three systems to find one bank statement.

codes.def: Tracing one sampled item to the documents that support it.
codes.include: Field-by-field comparison of record to document.
codes.example: Matching an invoice amount and date to the ledger line.

codes.def: Evidence that is partial, illegible or the wrong version.
codes.include: Any rework caused by the document itself.
codes.example: A scanned contract with the signature page missing.

codes.def: Client requests and the waiting they cause.
codes.include: Request raised, chased or re-raised.
codes.example: Second request for shipping documents after the first came back incomplete.

codes.def: Workpaper format or layout differs from what the reviewer expects.
codes.include: Reviewer time spent decoding layout before substance.
codes.example: Reviewer asks where the population summary is.

codes.def: Reference to evidence or another workpaper is missing or wrong.
codes.include: Review notes about references.
codes.example: Note: reference points at prior-year file.

codes.def: Work redone after review or after a finding.
codes.include: Any second pass on completed work.
codes.example: Sample retested after the population changed.

codes.def: Conclusion wording questioned or rewritten.
codes.include: Notes on how the conclusion is phrased.
codes.example: Conclusion does not state the assertion covered.

codes.def: A Test of Details structure adapted by hand from the methodology template.
codes.include: Any local variant of a standard structure.
codes.example: Team adds two columns to the standard structure and drops one.

codes.def: What the reviewer checks first.
codes.include: Explicit statements or observed first actions in review.
codes.example: Manager opens the evidence reference before reading the conclusion.

codes.def: Review note loops: raise, clear, re-raise.
codes.include: Any note that takes more than one pass to clear.
codes.example: Note cleared, then reopened by the partner.

codes.def: Waiting for review to happen.
codes.include: Time between ready for review and reviewed.
codes.example: Workpaper waits three days for the manager.

codes.def: Hesitation or extra checking before sign-off.
codes.include: Any statement about what the signer needs to see.
codes.example: Partner asks to see the exception resolution before signing.

codes.def: An exception is detected and recorded.
codes.include: The act of flagging, not the judgment.
codes.example: Amount differs from invoice by more than tolerance.

codes.def: Work to explain, waive or escalate an exception.
codes.include: Follow-up requests, calls, memos.
codes.example: Calling the client controller about a cutoff difference.

codes.def: Professional judgment applied to an exception.
codes.include: Statements that this step cannot be delegated.
codes.example: Whether a difference is a misstatement is my call.

codes.def: Busy season concentration of work.
codes.include: Statements about volume or hours in peak weeks.
codes.example: Everything lands in the same three weeks.

codes.def: Interruptions that break a tracing task.
codes.include: Any switch away from the task before it completes.
codes.example: Client call mid-sample; restart from the beginning.

codes.def: Context lost between roles or days.
codes.include: Any re-explanation of state at a handoff.
codes.example: Senior re-walks the sample for the manager.

codes.def: Work the person would hand to an agent.
codes.include: Explicit offers to delegate.
codes.example: It can do the matching. I will look at the differences.

codes.def: Work the person would never hand off.
codes.include: Explicit refusals.
codes.example: The conclusion is mine.

codes.def: What would make the person trust an agent's output.
codes.include: Conditions stated for trust.
codes.example: Show me the page it read.

codes.def: Accountability fear about agent errors.
codes.include: Statements about blame or liability.
codes.example: If it is wrong, it is still my name on the file.

codes.def: Wanting to reject or redo one step rather than the whole run.
codes.include: Any request for step-level control.
codes.example: I would rerun just the retrieval with the right file.

codes.def: Documentation requirements shaping the work.
codes.include: Statements about what the file must contain.
codes.example: The reviewer must be able to re-perform from the file.

codes.def: Independence shaping who may conclude.
codes.include: Statements that the auditor must conclude.
codes.example: A tool cannot sign.

codes.def: Data handling and access limits.
codes.include: Statements about what may be shared or stored where.
codes.example: That file cannot leave the client network.

themes.name: Locating evidence costs more than judging it
themes.statement: Auditors spend their effort finding and assembling evidence across systems and requests. The judgment, once the document is in front of them, is fast.
themes.boundary: Retrieval is the first candidate for the agent (Q1). What it retrieved must stay visible (Q3).

themes.name: Tracing a sample to its documents is the repetitive core
themes.statement: Field-by-field comparison of each sampled item to its documents is the bulk of fieldwork hours. It is procedural and it is where attention fades.
themes.boundary: Extraction and matching are agent work. The field-structure library defines what to match (D-06).

themes.name: Reviewers look for the source first, the conclusion second
themes.statement: Managers and partners open the evidence reference before they read the conclusion. A conclusion without a reachable source is not reviewable.
themes.boundary: Every claim carries a citation that opens the source at the span (D-03).

themes.name: Rework originates in references and format, not judgment
themes.statement: Review notes and second passes cluster on missing references, inconsistent layout and conclusion wording. Judgment calls are rarely the cause of rework.
themes.boundary: An agent that drafts with references and a fixed structure removes the common causes of rework without touching judgment.

themes.name: Review latency compounds under deadline and notes loop
themes.statement: Workpapers wait for review, then notes take more than one pass to clear. The waiting is where deadline pressure turns into shortcuts.
themes.boundary: Review needs a place with a queue and state, not a popup on a workpaper (D-04).

themes.name: Exceptions are where judgment lives and nobody hands that off
themes.statement: Detecting a difference is mechanical. Deciding what it means is professional judgment and every role names it as theirs.
themes.boundary: The agent detects and documents exceptions. Resolution is a human checkpoint by design, not by default.

themes.name: Trust requires seeing what the agent read and rejecting one step
themes.statement: Trust conditions are concrete: show the page, show the step, let me redo one step with the right input. A black box with a confidence number does not qualify.
themes.boundary: Step-level provenance and step-level rejection with rerun (D-13, D-14). Confidence shows its basis (D-08).

themes.name: Accountability fear: if it is wrong, it is my name
themes.statement: Auditors expect to carry the consequence of an agent's error. They will route around a tool that makes that risk invisible.
themes.boundary: Sign-off stays human-only with its own affordance (D-05). Failure is visible and recoverable (D-12).

themes.name: Teams want the system to enforce data limits
themes.statement: Rules about what may be shared with a tool are known by methodology and partially by teams. Teams would rather the product refuse than remember.
themes.boundary: Data classes with per-class agent permission, visible in the product (D-05, D-09).

themes.name: Format inconsistency slows review more than content does
themes.statement: Reviewers decode layout before substance. The same structure with the same fields in the same place would remove that step.
themes.boundary: Typed templates from the field-structure library fix the structure (D-06).

themes.name: Handoffs between roles and days lose context
themes.statement: State is re-explained at every handoff: what was tested, what is open, what was asked of the client. The context lives in people, not in the file.
themes.boundary: The agent timeline and run state carry context across handoffs. The run, not the person, holds the state.

themes.name: Experts want fewer clicks, not more guidance
themes.statement: Seniors and managers know the procedure. They want speed, keyboard operation and density. Explanatory UI slows them.
themes.boundary: Dense, keyboard-first layout (D-15). Guidance is progressive, never modal.

themes.name: Standard Test of Details structures are adapted by hand
themes.statement: The methodology defines the structures. Teams adapt them locally. The local variants are a rework and review source. Nobody wants variation; they want the structure to fit.
themes.boundary: The 60+ structures become typed templates the agent plans against (D-06). Fit is a property of the library, not a local hack.

evidence.finding: Effort concentrates on locating and assembling evidence, not on judging it.
Client requests and re-requests are the longest waits in fieldwork.
Field-by-field tracing of samples is the largest block of fieldwork hours.
Attention fades across a long tracing session; errors cluster late.
Reviewers open the evidence reference before reading the conclusion.
A conclusion whose source cannot be reached is sent back regardless of its content.
Rework causes cluster on references, format and wording rather than judgment.
Workpapers wait for review, and notes take more than one pass to clear.
Deadline pressure converts review waiting into shortcuts.
Detecting a difference is mechanical; deciding what it means is named as human work by every role.
Trust conditions are concrete: the page read, the step taken, the ability to redo one step.
A confidence number without its basis is distrusted by reviewers.
Auditors expect to carry the consequence of an agent's error and will route around a tool that hides the risk.
Data handling limits are known by methodology and partially by teams.
Teams prefer a product that refuses to one that relies on memory of the rules.
Reviewers decode layout before substance when formats vary.
State is re-explained at every handoff; the file does not hold it.
Experienced users want density, keyboard operation and speed over guidance.
Standard Test of Details structures are adapted locally and the variants cause rework.
Methodology reviewers want the structure to fit the procedure rather than be edited around it.
